newsitem.title: USA: General Mills sees record FY97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: General Mills sees record FY97 earnings.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Thursday that it expects to report record earnings for fiscal 1997.

Earlier, General Mills reported earnings for the second quarter ended November 24 of $1.00 a share, up from $0.92 a year ago. For the first six months, it earned $1.62 a share, including an $0.18 charge, down from $1.78 a year ago.
First-half results include about $0.16 of an expected $0.20 a share earnings impact from cuts in cereal prices. About $0.04 a share of that price-related earnings impact fell in the second quarter.
The impact of price cuts on future quarters will be less as promotional spending on established brands is reduced.

"Operating results for the first half excluding the impact of cereal pricing actions fully met our expectations," General Mills Chairman Steve Sanger said in a statement. "We expect to continue our progress in the second half toward our objective of delivering record earnings for fiscal 1997."
General Mills said its total domestic volume was up nine percent in the second quarter, with gains in every business unit.

Earnings from international operations grew 18 percent in the second quarter, led by its Cereal Partners Worldwide venture with Nestle SA. Through six months, Cereal Partners unit volume was up 17 percent.

In Canada, cereal volume grew 13 percent in the second quarter and 11 percent in the first half. That drove cereal market share for the year-to-date period up nearly two points to 16 percent, General Mills said.
Volume for Snack Ventures Europe, its PepsiCo Inc venture, was down slightly in the first half compared with the prior-year period that included heavy promotional activity.
International Dessert Partners, its venture ith CPC International Inc, is experiencing good consumer trial and distribution gains in its four initial Latin American markets.

General Mills reported earnings from joint ventures in the second quarter of $1.5 million, compared with a year-ago loss of $200,000. For the first half, venture earnings were $700,000, down from $900,000 a year before, due primarily to spending to launch the dessert venture.

General Mills said volume and market share performance was strong across its other domestic businesses. Helper dinner mix volume rose nine percent for the second quarter and 12 percent for the first half of the year.
Snack unit volume gained 12 percent in the quarter and three percent through the first half, led by strong initial performance from its new Golden Grahams Treats snack bars launched in October.
Yoplait-Colombo yogurt volume rose 12 percent in the quarter and market share was up two points.
Volume for Betty Crocker desserts, flour and baking mixes grew three percent in the quarter. Food service operations showed a seven percent volume rise.
